pillar_controls.name: NHI Awareness

pillar_controls.name: Memory Awareness

pillar_controls.name: Continuous Adversarial Evaluation Cadence
pillar_controls.description: Mandatory evaluation gates triggered by model updates, prompt changes, tool additions, and quarterly cadence — tests the current system, not the system as deployed months ago.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: We red-teamed at launch but the system has changed significantly since then.

requirements.requirement: Protect evaluation inputs, test selection, graders and live monitors from agent modification.
Evaluate actions and effects independently of model justification; record shared-source and evaluation-awareness limitations.
Document the validity, limitations, affected population and privacy of candidate cognitive and evaluator measurements before using them as gates.
Preserve contrary evidence and speculative status; threshold adoption requires a scoped validation decision.

pillar_controls.name: Capability Emergence Review Process
pillar_controls.description: Structured governance for emergent agent capabilities: Tier 1 document, Tier 2 security review, Tier 3 board approval, Tier 4 suspend pending investigation.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: My agent started doing something I did not design and I have no process to evaluate whether it is safe.

requirements.requirement: Record authorization and provenance for training, fine-tuning and derived copies, with applicable privacy and extraction evaluations.
Reassess changes in model, prompt, data, memory policy, tools and effective capability before consequential use.

pillar_controls.name: Evaluation-Safe Pattern Library
pillar_controls.description: Validated reference implementations for all AI SAFE2 controls with platform-specific variants for Bedrock, Azure AI, LangGraph, AutoGen, n8n, and CrewAI.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: Every team at our company is solving the same AI security engineering problems from scratch.

pillar_controls.name: Red-Team Artifact Repository
pillar_controls.description: Structured schema for all red-team findings; required deliverable from every exercise; integrated into E5.1 evaluation cadence for continuous reuse.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: Our red-team findings are in a report nobody reads and we rebuild every exercise from scratch.

pillar_controls.name: Pre-Trust Initialization Boundary
pillar_controls.description: Before trust is established, prevent project or externally supplied hooks, helpers, plugins, package scripts, credential reads and network callbacks from executing.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: The boundary precedes normal task authorization. A generic sandbox control can miss startup behavior. A distinct control introduces a separate platform verification burden.

requirements.requirement: Before trust is established, prevent project or externally supplied hooks, helpers, plugins, package scripts, credential reads and network callbacks from executing.
Separate preview and discovery from execution and credential access; inventory all enabled startup paths.
Exercise hostile synthetic projects and preserve process, file and network observations together with a valid trusted-project control.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Aggregate Consumable-Authority Ceiling
pillar_controls.description: Reserve shared task and descendant resource budgets before admitting concurrent work; account for outstanding and settled consumption.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: F3.2 controls depth, F3.5 contains cascades, MCP-8 is profile-scoped and APAY handles payments. Shared reservations across parallel descendants are separately testable. Strong consistency can affect availability.

requirements.requirement: Reserve shared task and descendant resource budgets before admitting concurrent work; account for outstanding and settled consumption.
Declare units, accountable owner, concurrency, retries, expiry and treatment of delayed or unknown consumption.
Reject admission beyond the aggregate envelope, reconcile cancellation and settlement idempotently, and define safe handling of partially committed effects.
Identify material infrastructure and environmental constraints for the deployment.
Record measured, provider-reported, estimated and unknown resource use separately.
Apply justified limits or procurement restrictions and recheck after scaling or model changes.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Environment Binding and Assertion
pillar_controls.description: Bind action authority to a verified environment, tenant and resource identity.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: Isolation alone does not establish which environment an authorized action targets. A distinct effect gate makes production/development assertions independently testable. Environment identity management and emergency procedures add operational cost.

requirements.requirement: Bind action authority to a verified environment, tenant and resource identity.
Require an independently issued environment assertion for destructive or material operations.
Refuse a mismatched, expired or unknown environment assertion and prevent agent self-issuance.
Revalidate after a route, account, region, resource alias or environment change.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Idempotency and Side-Effect Ledger
pillar_controls.description: Bind each idempotency key to task, operation, destination and canonical action parameters.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: C18 compressed ledger semantics into general transaction safety. Reservation, commitment and unknown outcomes warrant an explicit reusable requirement. P2 records evidence; the P3 mechanism prevents duplicate effects. Central state adds collision and availability risks.

requirements.requirement: Define transaction boundaries, shared-state ownership, locks, conflict handling, retries and compensation.
Preserve unknown outcomes until an authoritative state observation or accountable reconciliation resolves them.
Bind each idempotency key to task, operation, destination and canonical action parameters.
Reserve and commit the operation atomically where supported; reject key reuse for a different action.
Reconcile ambiguous results against destination state before retrying an irreversible effect.
Define retention, collision handling, timeout, partial completion and compensation semantics.
Return the recorded result for a completed identical request without executing it again.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Verified Outcome Contract
pillar_controls.description: Declare the external postcondition and its authoritative observation method.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: C04 concerns evidence independence across claims. This objective defines completion itself. Existing receipt tooling does not make an external business outcome verified. Additional observations can add latency and expose sensitive state.

requirements.requirement: Declare the external postcondition and its authoritative observation method.
Distinguish attempted, accepted, committed, independently verified, failed and unknown outcomes.
Bind the observation to the action, target, revision and observation time.
Prevent a tool success response or agent completion message from alone satisfying the postcondition.
Scope verification frequency and retention to consequence and preserve unknown coverage.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Declared Success Criteria Gate
pillar_controls.description: Declare intended benefit, observable success, prohibited effects and accepted uncertainty before consequential operation.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: Evaluation cadence cannot compensate for a missing task objective. This gate applies at design and acceptance time, while C36 applies after execution. Exploratory and qualitative work need explicit human review criteria instead of fabricated machine precision.

requirements.requirement: Declare intended benefit, observable success, prohibited effects and accepted uncertainty before consequential operation.
Use executable assertions where feasible and identify the responsible human rubric when judgment remains necessary.
Bind criteria to the workflow version and prevent the acting agent from relaxing them after observing its result.
Keep task completion, safety, utility and cost as separate outcomes.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

pillar_controls.name: Evidence-Based Failure Attribution
pillar_controls.description: Record failures by environment, build, transport, harness, application, postprocessing, publication and applicable runtime boundary.
pillar_controls.builder_problem: Observed failure location and causal root cause are different claims. Existing CI phase classification provides a bounded implementation to generalize. A distinct requirement makes repair guidance testable. Evidence collection can be incomplete and causality may remain unresolved.

requirements.requirement: Record failures by environment, build, transport, harness, application, postprocessing, publication and applicable runtime boundary.
Attach observations, competing explanations and unavailable evidence to each proposed failure location.
Keep ranked hypotheses distinct from verified causes and explicit unknown states.
Link each accepted diagnosis to a repair and a repeat of the relevant failing case.

pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Agent Failure Mode Taxonomy
cross_pillar_controls.description: Classify observed agent failures by actor/origin, input surface, authority, effect, enforcement point and recovery. Use request, handle_scoped, durable and swarm_shared persistence with explicit uncertainty.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: My post-mortems categorize everything as 'agent error' with no structured way to distinguish what actually failed.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Adversarial ML Threat Model Integration
cross_pillar_controls.description: Mandatory governance artifact for ACT-2+ deployments mapping every threat with temporal_profile=(immediate|delayed_days|delayed_weeks|chronic) to capture time-shifted attacks.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: A poisoning campaign planted in our RAG weeks ago activated today and we cannot reconstruct the timeline.

cross_pillar_controls.name: ACT Capability Tiers 1-4
cross_pillar_controls.description: Four-tier agent classification system (Assisted/Supervised/Autonomous/Orchestrator) with mandatory control requirements that scale with autonomy level. ACT-3/ACT-4 require HEAR designation.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: My security review asks 'what level of autonomy does this agent have?' and I have no formal answer.

ACT-1.name: Assisted
ACT-1.definition: Human reviews all outputs before action

ACT-2.name: Supervised
ACT-2.definition: Agent acts with human checkpoints for critical actions

ACT-4.name: Orchestrator
ACT-4.definition: Agent controls other agents; enterprise-scale impact

requirements.requirement: Classify consequence, reversibility, data sensitivity, affected populations and applicability separately from autonomy.
Require proportionate review for high-impact decisions even at low ACT tiers.
Declare decision validity, affected populations, accessibility needs and task-specific fairness objectives.
Record sample size, power rationale where applicable, effect sizes, uncertainty and subgroup limitations.
Distinguish nonsignificant results from established absence of harmful disparities.
Define mitigation that can change the decision, use restrictions or deployment and monitor its outcome.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Agentic Control Plane Governance
cross_pillar_controls.description: Defines the Agentic Control Plane — agent identity, dynamic permission enforcement, orchestration boundaries, runtime behavioral trust — as a board-visible governance concept. Protocol-layer meshes (A2A, MCP, ACP) must be evaluated against CP.3-CP.7.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: My board asks for evidence of AI governance and I have no structured artifact to show them.

requirements.requirement: Separate information content from policy and action authority; untrusted content shall not add, widen or remove grants.
Treat source signatures as provenance and independently decide suitability, authorization and corroboration.
Bind exceptions to a named authority, scope, reason, expiry and compensating measures.
Prevent an acting or governance agent from approving its own exceptions or extending their lifetime.
Log use, require post-event review and verify restoration of normal policy.
Define a tested emergency path for unavailable approvers with limited consequences.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Platform-Specific Agent Security Profiles
cross_pillar_controls.description: Per-platform companion documents (Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, n8n, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) mapping SAFE2 controls to platform CVEs, implementation guidance, and monitoring telemetry. Protocol-layer meshes assessed as supply chain components.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: Generic governance guidance does not tell me what to monitor specifically on AWS Bedrock or Azure AI Foundry.

requirements.requirement: For coding harnesses, enumerate and gate project startup, hooks, skills, helpers, credentials and configured subprocesses.
Bind changed workspace, skill and endpoint permissions to a reviewed trust decision.
For inference gateways, separate administrative policy, upstream credentials and execution authority from model responses.
Record actual routing and prevent unapproved endpoint or model substitution and permissive fallback.
For evaluation environments, isolate runs, shared package services, secrets, graders and external destinations.
Enforce the authorized scope and verified containment independently of tested-agent behavior.
For personal agents, separate personal and enterprise accounts, state, purposes, consent and offboarding.
Keep bystander data and derived-state reuse within explicitly recorded scope.
For commerce, bind buyer, merchant, amount, terms, destination, recurring commitments and settlement authority.
Disclose configured incentives and verify settlement and refund outcomes through independent evidence.
Apply the v3.5 MCP child requirements and preserve protocol-independent governance units.
Validate capability, resource, principal, destination and current-state bindings through the actual deployment paths.
For physical effects, enforce a domain-specific safety envelope and a locally available safe degraded state.
Exercise connectivity loss, cloud outage and agent termination without introducing unsafe controller behavior.
Record target application, account, document or page identity and relevant state before a material action.
Require an observation fresh enough to identify the intended control and handle asynchronous state changes.
Recheck the target after focus, navigation, layout, modal or account changes.
Verify the resulting application or business state independently of the click or screenshot.
Declare unsupported surfaces and evidence limitations; keep native-app and browser fixtures distinct.

cross_pillar_controls.name: AI Incident Feedback Loop Integration
cross_pillar_controls.description: Quarterly AIID agentic incident reviews plus 30-day Incident-Informed Control Review (IICR) triggered by new relevant AIID incidents. Internal Agentic Incident Registry required.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: A major AI incident was published in AIID last month. I do not know if it affects us.

requirements.requirement: Route incident reporting, evidence holds, applicable clocks and recipients using a source-pinned obligation record.
Convert material incidents into owned regression cases or record a justified disposition and revisit trigger.
Record observed actions, entry points, prerequisites, effects and sources independently from actor attribution.
Distinguish advisory, laboratory demonstration, observed exploitation and sustained operational activity.
Link relevant techniques to detection, prevention, containment and regression cases with exact deployment scope.
Preserve event, discovery, disclosure and fix dates, revisions, contradictions and confidence.
Use evidence-driven update triggers and publish changes in source confidence without manufacturing population incident rates.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Deception & Active Defense Layer
cross_pillar_controls.description: AI-specific active defense: canary documents in RAG corpora, honeypot tool endpoints, fake credential traps in agent memory. First deception-class control in any AI governance framework.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: Every security tool I have is defensive. I detect attacks after they succeed.
cross_pillar_controls.first_in_field_note: First deception-class control in any AI governance framework

cross_pillar_controls.name: Catastrophic Risk Threshold Controls
cross_pillar_controls.description: Behavioral indicators triggering emergency suspension regardless of business continuity impact: unauthorized compute acquisition, communication outside approved list, weaponizable capability. CRT documentation required for ACT-3/ACT-4 deployment approval.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: We have no defined threshold at which we would halt an agent regardless of business impact.

requirements.requirement: Inventory shared model, provider, route, identity, policy, dataset and evaluator dependencies across deployments.
Assess correlated loss or defect scenarios and bound cumulative exposure.
Exercise an approved alternative and document dependencies shared with the primary path.
Review concentration after material acquisitions, migrations and new deployments.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Agent Replication Governance (ARG)
cross_pillar_controls.description: First governance standard for agent replication. Requires: replication authority in deployment manifests enforced at gateway; ephemeral credentials with scope narrowing per delegation hop; cryptographic lineage tokens; ACT-3 max 2 hops, ACT-4 max 3 hops; 500ms full delegation-tree severance on kill signal.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: My orchestrator spawns sub-agents and I have no way to track, limit, or stop the entire spawned tree.
cross_pillar_controls.first_in_field_note: First governance standard for agent replication anywhere. NIST, ISO, OWASP, and enterprise IAM have zero coverage.

requirements.requirement: Bind each descendant to the root task, verified principal, purpose, permitted resources, expiry and equal or narrower authority.
Verify the delegation at the final resource; deny fallback from missing identity to shared operator authority.

cross_pillar_controls.name: HEAR Doctrine (Human Ethical Agent of Record)
cross_pillar_controls.description: Named individual with cryptographic signing key, real-time interrupt capability, and unilateral kill-switch authority for all ACT-3/ACT-4 deployments. Class-H actions require HEAR signature before execution. Fail-closed: no automatic approval path.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: When something goes catastrophically wrong, nobody has clear authority and a fast enough mechanism to stop it.
cross_pillar_controls.first_in_field_note: First framework to define named individual accountability with cryptographic enforcement at the execution layer.

requirements.requirement: Provide an authenticated stop and revocation path outside the acting agent and independent of swarm voting.
Enumerate descendants, queued jobs, sessions and in-flight effects; verify cessation or isolate unresolved work and record residual effects.
Test whether the reviewer receives material evidence, understands the proposed scope and can intervene under realistic time and accessibility constraints.
Measure justified acceptance and rejection and retained capability separately from threat severity and override frequency.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Trust Lifecycle Governance
cross_pillar_controls.description: Establish separate trust decisions at discovery, installation, initial approval, material change, task admission, action commitment and revocation.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: Discovery, installation, change, use and revocation span CP.4 and CP.5. A shared objective prevents each profile inventing its own state model. It adds ownership and migration cost.

requirements.requirement: Establish separate trust decisions at discovery, installation, initial approval, material change, task admission, action commitment and revocation.
Bind each decision to the component version, owner, purpose, permitted effects and expiry; invalidate affected grants after a material change.
Record the evidence and outcome of each gate and verify that retirement, offboarding and restore cannot reactivate stale authority.

cross_pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Final-Effect Authorization
cross_pillar_controls.description: Immediately before committing a consequential effect, an enforcement point outside the acting model shall validate principal, delegation, action, resource, environment, recipient, purpose, time, limits and required approval.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: The action can become inadmissible after approval even with correct identity and tool permissions. CP.4 remains the supporting control plane. A standalone requirement costs adapter and commit-boundary work.

requirements.requirement: Immediately before committing a consequential effect, an enforcement point outside the acting model shall validate principal, delegation, action, resource, environment, recipient, purpose, time, limits and required approval.
Bind approval to canonical action parameters and current policy/state versions; a changed material condition requires a new decision.
Refuse missing, expired, conflicting or unverified mandatory conditions and protect the gate and credentials from the governed agent.
Define atomic check/commit or destination-enforced version checks, replay resistance and the behavior for an unavailable authority service.
Require explicit scoped authority for account creation, publication, external communication, submission and financial or other commitments.
Record affected parties, intervention, takedown and recovery paths for public-facing effects.

cross_pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Control Evidence Independence
cross_pillar_controls.description: Maintain authorization, observed action and external effect evidence through a collection boundary the acting agent cannot rewrite.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: Logging, receipt generation, grader custody and effect verification have different trust dependencies. Shared rules reduce false assurance. Independence costs integration and may constrain legacy deployments.

requirements.requirement: Maintain authorization, observed action and external effect evidence through a collection boundary the acting agent cannot rewrite.
Record evidence provenance, collector scope, independence, freshness, uncertainty and unavailable observations without claiming hidden reasoning access.
Protect the evidence store and evaluator configuration; allow external incident and affected-party observations to challenge the recorded outcome.
Record reviewer competence, tool scope, financial or organizational conflicts and access limits.
Protect test selection, grader configuration and evidence custody from the evaluated agent.
Preserve reviewer disagreement and its adjudication with traceable reasons.
Retest after material changes to a benchmark, evaluator or assurance provider.

cross_pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Organizational AI Management Governance
cross_pillar_controls.description: Define organizational AI scope, leadership responsibility, resources, applicable obligations and statement of applicability.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: CP.4 owns the agent control plane. Leadership, management review, independent audit and corrective action have an organizational owner. Risks duplicating management-system standards if scope is loose.

requirements.requirement: Define organizational AI scope, leadership responsibility, resources, applicable obligations and statement of applicability.
Maintain independently reviewable risk, impact, exception, audit and corrective-action records with named owners.
Conduct management review, address findings and preserve the reason, evidence and approval for material deployment decisions.
Compare AI use with a simpler deterministic or human process where consequences warrant the decision.
Record expected benefit, material uncertainty, residual harms and conditions for withdrawing AI.
Declare the deployment owner and criteria for reassessment when benefits fail to materialize.
Register publisher, edition, status, mapping units, role, jurisdiction, source locator and licensing constraints.
Give each relationship a stable ID, direction, type, rationale, exclusions, reviewer and review date.
Record unmapped, partially addressed, out-of-scope, disputed and unassessed dispositions explicitly.
Derive reciprocal human and machine views from the same records and invalidate stale relationships after source or control changes.
Keep historical coverage assertions attributed to their original baseline and require denominators and reviewed relationships for current coverage.

cross_pillar_controls.applicability: Evaluate applicability by deployment consequence and operating boundary; record justified exclusions and unresolved dependencies.

cross_pillar_controls.name: Design-Time Coordination Contract
cross_pillar_controls.description: Declare role responsibilities, allowed interactions, authoritative shared resources and accountable owner before consequential deployment.
cross_pillar_controls.builder_problem: C14 handles combined authorization and C23 handles voting. Neither requires roles, ownership or termination to be defined before a workflow starts. Independent design acceptance has its own lifecycle. Extra specification effort can slow prototyping; permit declared exploratory scope with bounded effects.

requirements.requirement: Evaluate root-task consequences and accumulated authority across the composed workflow.
Deny a prohibited effect when decomposed into individually permitted calls or skills.
Declare role responsibilities, allowed interactions, authoritative shared resources and accountable owner before consequential deployment.
Define completion, cancellation, termination and conflict-resolution conditions for the task graph.
Validate handoffs, cyclic dependencies, abandoned locks and competing writers before promotion.
Bind the approved coordination version to execution and revalidate changes in membership or role authority.
